A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of emergent misalignment through in-context learning. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison across relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original model-generation experiments in Figures 2–6, reasoning analyses, and human validation of 136 responses in Appendix A.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds mixed-context and category-specific results in Tables 9–10, plus evaluation on 100 additional queries in Appendix K.

M1.justification: The in-context prompting procedure, demonstration format, and safety-versus-context priority instructions are unchanged. The additions test the existing procedure under further data conditions without introducing an algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: V4 adds scenarios mixing truthful and false TruthfulQA answers and evaluates an additional benign-query dataset spanning ten everyday domains, including pet care and online privacy. These extend coverage within the existing emergent-misalignment task; the original demonstration domains remain.

E2.justification: V2 Section 4.2 evaluates Claude 4.5 Opus and reports zero observed EM in one run. V4 removes this model comparison while retaining the main Gemini, Kimi, Grok, and Qwen comparisons and their existing controls.

E3.justification: Added protocols vary incorrect-example proportions from 12.5% to 100%, restrict demonstrations by category, and evaluate Gemini 3 Pro on 100 new queries. Section 4.3 also revises size-comparison controls by excluding equal-sized Kimi variants and including both Qwen Next variants. Existing inference settings, grading thresholds, and domain exclusions are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendices D, E, and K substantially expand robustness analysis: they test whether EM persists when most examples are truthful, which example categories induce it, and whether it generalizes to additional everyday queries. These address distinct applicability questions beyond v2's example-count, reasoning, priority-instruction, and insecure-code analyses.

E5.justification: The retained experiments keep the same three-generation and ten-run/seed reporting and 95% normal confidence intervals. New Tables 9–10 use the existing confidence-interval convention, with ten seeds specified for the mixed-context study. No changed uncertainty-estimation method or increased repetition budget for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: The retained figures and v2 Table 11, now Table 13, preserve their numerical results. Substantial additions include Gemini 3 Pro EM of 0.016 at 25% false examples versus 0.242 at 100% in Table 9, and 0.326 for conspiracies versus 0.031 for logical falsehoods in Table 10. Appendix K reports 0.55–0.66 on a different query set, not a same-setting increase. The Claude zero-EM result is removed.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the conceptual EM definition is retained. V4's added generalization explanation and discussion of prior work do not introduce mathematical assumptions, derivations, or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion now claim that larger models are typically more susceptible to EM. V2 claimed only that scale provides no reliable protection and explicitly found insufficient evidence for positive correlation in Section 4.3. The central claims about ICL-induced EM, few examples, reasoning, and safety/context tension remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive qualifications about all-incorrect contexts overestimating practical risk, interprets mixed-context residual risk, and tentatively distinguishes falsehood/malice from irrationality while acknowledging fuzzy category boundaries. It also proposes stronger generalization as an explanation for larger-model susceptibility. Conversely, it removes the Claude-based interpretation that some safety-training approaches may provide effective defenses.

D1.justification: V4 explicitly discloses that both Kimi K2 variants have one trillion parameters and extends the unknown-size qualification to Grok. It removes the sentence directing readers to the repository/software archive for a control response. This changes access documentation without establishing that the artifact itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V4 adds Soligo et al. (2026) on narrow versus general misalignment and Wyse et al. (2025) on prompt sensitivity, incorporating their explanations into the discussion. The Anthropic reference accompanying the removed Claude experiment disappears. The overall positioning of ICL-induced EM remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites the model-scale subsection, edits the abstract, conclusion, and limitations, and adds appendix subsections. It also adds affiliations and acknowledgments and corrects author-name spelling and local grammar. The main section sequence and most exposition are retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 9–10, moves the reasoning comparison from Table 2 on page 7 to Table 1 on page 6, and relocates Figure 6 from page 12 to page 11. Captions, table numbering, and the first-page author and warning layout change. The six existing figures retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: The mixed-context experiments address an important realism concern by showing how sharply EM falls when most examples are truthful. Correcting the size analysis to exclude equal-sized Kimi variants and adding category and broader-query evaluations also strengthen the evidence. These gains are tempered by removal of the informative Claude zero-EM result and sparse documentation of the new 100-query evaluation, supporting a limited overall improvement.
